run.note: A scratch --data-root, never ~/.ai-raccoon. Driven over stdio MCP by scratchpad/mcpcli.py.

derived.note: Counted from the tree, then CONFIRMED against the live server's tools/list and prompts/list.

integration-review.note: The campaign's Phase 7 join review, run on the MERGED tree rather than on any branch.
integration-review.seams-present: ChunkToBudgetAsync, WriteChunks.InsertAsync, BundledProvider, IShareExtractService, IQueryGuardService, IMemoryWriteService, agent-requested-share, ObservableTime, UnexpectedText — every one still on main after four squash merges
integration-review.dispatch-not-just-compile: MemoryTools.Write -> writes.WriteAsync; Search -> queryGuard.EvaluateAsync; ShareExtract -> shareExtract.RunAsync; and NO tool calls store.WriteAsync directly any more. A wiring that compiles but never dispatches is the named join hazard, so it was checked by call site and then again live below.

items.expected-result: Release pack succeeds; the global tool updates and reports derived.version
items.evidence: 9 packages incl. all 7 RIDs | updated from '1.14.1' to '1.15.0' | 1.15.0+aa51b34d1070a95729b38570c11c640038871636

items.expected-result: `serve --port 0` binds and reports its port; `--restart` cycles the incumbent
items.evidence: Now listening on: http://127.0.0.1:50169 | http://127.0.0.1:50169/mcp | 'the server on port 50169 (pid 16878) stopped and the port is free' then bound again
items.observed-result: Both halves observed; the incumbent named by pid.
items.acceptation-reason: Restart confirmed the port free before rebinding.

items.expected-result: 26 tools, 2 prompts, serverInfo reports the release version
items.observed-result: Live surface matches the tree-derived counts.
items.acceptation-reason: Counts derived FIRST, then confirmed — neither copied from the other.

items.expected-result: A long body stores as multiple in-budget rows with no text lost (ADR-0064)
items.evidence: 29,200-char body -> 40 rows under one path, max chunk 1,076 chars, 34,543 chars total across rows (overlap accounts for the excess)
items.observed-result: Chunked live through a real server. Before this release the same body stored as ONE row of 8,123 BERT tokens against a 256-token window.
items.acceptation-reason: Row count read from the bank directly, not inferred from memory_list — which lists FILES and showed one entry either way.

items.expected-result: memory_write(context:'shared') creates no shared row, lands in the caller's project, and queues a candidate (ADR-0067)
items.evidence: write -> {context: 'project:release115', stored: true, reason: 'queued-for-promotion: agent-requested-share'} | memory_promotion_list -> one row, score 1, reasons ['agent-requested-share']
items.observed-result: Every acceptance criterion of WP2 observed end to end: no shared row, project-scoped storage, a queued candidate distinguishable by its reason, and a response that says what happened.
items.acceptation-reason: This is the strongest form of the join review — the tool, the Core service and the queue exercised together through a real MCP session.

items.expected-result: A write returns stored:true with a content-derived hash and path
items.evidence: stored: true with distinct content-derived hash/path

items.expected-result: A natural-language query returns the written entry with ranking and snippet
items.observed-result: Top hit is the written entry; the search_quality row this release still reaps is written.
items.acceptation-reason: Hit checked by hash, not snippet text.

items.expected-result: memory_get returns the exact stored value
items.evidence: byte-exact round trip of the written content
items.acceptation-reason: Compared against the string written in the same session.

items.expected-result: An ingested file is chunked and a file#section query returns its chunks
items.evidence: ingest {"indexed":1}; anchored query returned chunks of that exact ADR carrying sourceFile
items.observed-result: Passes once the ingest scope is added.
items.acceptation-reason: First attempt returned path-outside-scope — CORRECT, the allowlist is empty by default. Documented precondition, not a workaround.

items.expected-result: A write matching a noise policy is refused with stored:false and a named reason
items.evidence: the '[IMPORTANT: Background process' and 'received signal' shapes are both refused with reason 'rejected by noise policy HermesBackgroundProcessLog'
items.acceptation-reason: A shape the policy does NOT name is stored — correct, and checked against HermesProcessNoisePolicy rather than assumed.

items.expected-result: Log-like queries are annotated; machine-output queries are refused
items.evidence: warn tier returns results plus the ADR-0040 guidance; refuse tier returns invalid-params with its guidance
items.observed-result: Both tiers fire. Now served by QueryGuardService in Core (ADR-0065) rather than by MemoryTools, and the behaviour is identical.
items.acceptation-reason: This is the live confirmation that WP8's extraction did not change what a caller sees.

items.expected-result: memory_watch_add registers a watch and status reports it
items.evidence: add -> {projectId, path}; status -> the watch present
items.observed-result: Passes once watching is enabled and scoped; before that, a typed 'watching-disabled' refusal.
items.acceptation-reason: The disabled path refuses typed rather than crashing.

items.evidence: stats {entries, pending, contexts}; promotion_list carries the agent-requested row above
items.observed-result: Both answer, and the queue now has real content because of WP2.

items.expected-result: The maintenance pass logs its registered event ids, including 522-524
items.observed-result: Four ids confirmed. 522-524 — the retention reapers — were NOT exercised: their pass runs on the maintenance cadence and a bank minutes old has nothing to purge.
items.acceptation-reason: Unchanged from 1.14.0 and honest: RetentionReaperTests covers the purge; what stays unverified live is that the hosted service reaches those ids on a real cadence.

items.expected-result: An unrecognised verb fails with a parse error and a non-zero exit
items.evidence: fixed in 1.14.1 by ADR-0060; exit 9 (FailedToParseCliArgs), nothing launched
items.acceptation-reason: Regression-covered by AppRunnerUnrecognisedVerbTests; not re-driven by hand here because the unit gate asserts the exit code directly.
